title: Leonardo da Vinci: Renaissance Master
description: One portrait, one mind—five steps from a famous smile to the secrets in the notebooks.

questions.question: What is Leonardo's most famous painting, known for its subject's mysterious smile?
questions.hint: It's of a woman with an enigmatic smile, housed in the Louvre
questions.explanation: The portrait in the Louvre—likely Lisa Gherardini—became the anchor for everything Leonardo tried to understand about light, flesh, and expression.

questions.question: Leonardo blended tones on the Mona Lisa using what technique (Italian for 'smoke')?
questions.hint: Soft, hazy transitions with no hard outlines—like smoke dissolving into air
questions.explanation: Sfumato let Leonardo dissolve edges around the Mona Lisa's eyes and mouth—the haze that makes her smile seem to shift when you look away.

questions.question: Leonardo's sfumato studies fill notebooks written in what reversed script?
questions.hint: You need a mirror to read it normally—written from right to left
questions.explanation: Thousands of pages run backward in his hand—perhaps to deter snooping, perhaps because the left-handed scribe found it faster.

questions.question: In those mirror-written notebooks, Leonardo sketched what bird-like flying machine?
questions.hint: A machine with flapping wings like a bird, from Greek words for 'bird' and 'wing'
questions.explanation: The ornithopter design—human-powered flapping wings—sat in the same codices as his sfumato notes and anatomy studies.

questions.question: Leonardo's ornithopter sketches share notebook space with anatomy drawn from what hands-on practice on human bodies?
questions.hint: Opening cadavers to study what lies beneath the skin
questions.explanation: Myth says he snuck corpses at night. Actually, he dissected around 30 bodies with permission at hospitals like Florence's Santa Maria Nuova—his drawings of the heart were centuries ahead of medicine.

imageHint: Sketches and inventions of a mind centuries ahead of its time

deeperMode.title: The Obsessive Perfectionist
deeperMode.description: Leonardo's relentless pursuit of knowledge and his unfinished masterpieces

questions.question: Leonardo was notorious for leaving works unfinished. Approximately how many paintings did he complete in his lifetime?
questions.hint: Fewer than twenty - his perfectionism often prevented him from finishing

questions.question: What did Leonardo call the phenomenon where distant objects appear blue or hazy?
questions.hint: A technique that shows depth by making distant objects appear less distinct and bluer
